title: Quantum-Enhanced AI and Machine Learning: Transforming Predictive Analytics
journal_or_venue: Recent Advances in Electrical & Electronic Engineering
abstract_summary: This review investigates how quantum computing can enhance AI and machine learning for predictive analytics, proposing a quantum-AI framework and hybrid quantum-classical workflows. Using frameworks such as Qiskit, TensorFlow Quantum, and PennyLane on finance, healthcare, and climate datasets, the paper reports improved accuracy and reduced training/simulation times (e.g., finance accuracy from 85% to 92%; healthcare diagnosis accuracy 94% with 50% faster training; climate modeling with 90% improved accuracy and 20% faster simulations).
methodology_description: The paper reports a hybrid quantum-classical experimental methodology in which classical components perform data ingestion and preprocessing and quantum components handle optimization and predictive tasks. The authors state they used real-world datasets from finance (market trends, risk data), healthcare (genomic sequences and diagnostic imaging) and climate modeling (atmospheric simulations), obtained from public repositories and industry case studies. The generic experiment flow described is: classical preprocessing (cleaning, outlier removal, normalization), feature selection, mapping/encoding of features for quantum algorithms, model training using quantum-enhanced algorithms (and hybrid quantum-classical pipelines), and evaluation against classical baselines on accuracy, computation time and scalability. Software frameworks named include Qiskit, TensorFlow Quantum and PennyLane for quantum work, and scikit-learn and TensorFlow for classical preprocessing and baselines. Experiments were run in a hybrid cloud environment with access to quantum processors. Specific low-level experimental details (dataset sizes, exact encoding, qubit counts, circuit depths, optimizer choices, number of shots, and exact QPU models) are not reported in the manuscript.
experimental_setup: Hybrid quantum-classical setup run in a hybrid cloud environment with access to quantum processors. Classical preprocessing and baseline training executed using standard CPU/GPU-based toolchains (Python, scikit-learn, TensorFlow); quantum model training and hybrid routines executed through Qiskit / TensorFlow Quantum / PennyLane connected to cloud quantum backends or simulators.

results_summary: The paper reports that quantum-enhanced AI and hybrid quantum-classical models produced improved predictive performance in three illustrative domains: finance (reported accuracy increase from 85% to 92%), healthcare (94% diagnostic accuracy and 50% reduction in training time), and climate modeling (reported '90% improved accuracy' and 20% faster simulation). The authors used Qiskit, TensorFlow Quantum, and PennyLane in hybrid experiments and argue that quantum algorithms (QSVM, QNN, QAOA) can better handle high-dimensional data and optimization tasks. The manuscript also highlights practical constraints — NISQ hardware limits, decoherence, gate errors, and costly quantum error correction — and frames hybrid integration and domain-specific quantum algorithm development as the next steps. While numeric improvements are reported, methodological detail and reproducibility are limited in the text.

key_ideas: #idea:quantum-advantage — Reported higher predictive accuracy in finance (85% -> 92%), healthcare (88% -> 94%) and claimed training/simulation speedups (50% training time reduction; 20% simulation time reduction).

#idea:hybrid-approach — Advocates hybrid quantum-classical workflows: classical preprocessing and feature selection, quantum modules for feature-mapping/optimization/prediction using Qiskit, TensorFlow Quantum, and PennyLane.
#idea:near-term-feasibility — Positions quantum-enhanced ML as NISQ-era applicable via variational QNN/QSVM/QAOA and cloud-accessible quantum backends.
#limitation:no-empirical-validation — The paper omits dataset identifiers, code, hardware specs, hyperparameters and low-level experiment details, making reproduction impossible from the manuscript.
#limitation:data-encoding — Describes data encoding/embedding conceptually but provides no specifics or cost/complexity analysis for encoding financial data into quantum states.
#limitation:qubit-count — No qubit counts, circuit depths or QPU models are reported, so it's unclear whether claimed results scale to realistic problem sizes.
#limitation:noise — Does not report noise levels or error-mitigation strategies; hardware noise impacts are not assessed.

#limitation:simulation-only — Experiments are described as run in hybrid cloud with 'access to quantum processors' but lack hardware provenance, leaving open the possibility results derive from simulators rather than physical QPUs.
contradictions: contradiction:scalability — The paper claims scalability improvements and even suggests exponential speedups for high-dimensional ML, but provides no low-level experimental evidence (no dataset sizes, qubit counts, circuit depths) to support these scaling claims.

contradiction:classical-vs-quantum — The review reports quantum models outperform classical baselines but fails to specify the baseline algorithms, hyperparameters or rigorous benchmarking procedures; thus the asserted quantum superiority is not substantiated by reproducible comparative evidence.
